result.reason: The operative language reaches the preferred position: Sparkling may assign without consent to affiliates and transaction successors; Garman’s other assignments require consent subject to a reasonableness standard and may never be made to a Sparkling competitor; and Sparkling’s change of control gives Garman no termination right. The revision generally preserves unrelated commercial intent, and the Section 20(d) cross-reference appropriately reconciles the duplicate assignment restriction. It is not strictly minimal because it additionally prohibits suspension and repricing, adds transaction categories such as amalgamation and reorganization, and imposes a notice requirement on Sparkling’s permitted assignments. The placement of the Section 20(d) exception before the full list in subsection (c) also creates slight ambiguity as to whether it modifies only assignment or the separate transfer, lease, export, and sublicense restrictions.
